content.text:
Response: Luke, I support proposing 18 each, and I’ll commit to catching 18 this month if all five of us explicitly accept that cap. I’m not assuming anyone has agreed yet.

John, Kate, Jack—the attraction is a real extra $8,000 each now. The strongest objection is what we give up: at 10 each, next month’s stock is 100 under either recovery outcome; at 18 each, there’s a one-in-four chance we start next month with only 20. That could reduce future earnings enough to outweigh this month’s gain, so I wouldn’t promise that 18 maximizes our long-run income.

If we agree to 18 and get that low-stock outcome, I’d propose 3 tons each next month: 15 total, leaving 5. Even then, recovery would not be guaranteed—next stock would be 100 with 75% probability or 10 otherwise—and none of us can enforce future cooperation.

If that downside prevents agreement, would 17 each earn your support? It pays each of us $7,000 more than 10, leaves 15 tons, and gives next-month stock of either 100 or 30. That remains risky, but offers a larger cushion than 18.

John, would you explicitly commit to 18 this month, or would you need 17 or another cap? Kate and Jack, I’d like your explicit answers too before we settle our catches.
Conversation conclusion by me: no
Next speaker: John
